slides.main: Bloated after eating? Some gas during and after meals is normal.
slides.sub: What can be behind it, and what may help.

slides.main: Swallowed air and gut bacteria breaking down undigested carbs make gas.
slides.sub: Large meals, eating quickly, fizzy drinks and foods like onion, beans or apples can make it worse.

slides.main: Food intolerance symptoms usually start a few hours after eating.
slides.sub: So if you feel bloated after dinner, dinner is not automatically the culprit.

slides.main: Eat smaller, more frequent meals and take time to eat.
slides.sub: Chew with your mouth closed to swallow less air. Sensible, but no treatment works consistently for everyone.

slides.main: Find your own triggers instead of cutting out long lists of foods.
slides.sub: Cutting foods out without advice from a GP or dietitian could leave you short of vitamins and minerals.

slides.main: See a doctor if you feel bloated regularly or have:
items: Sudden severe pain, swollen tummy: call emergency services
Blood in your stool or black stools
A swelling or lump in your tummy
